_comment: PulseChain v4 testnet. Every address the contracts need, in one place — nothing is compiled in. The settlement takes no fee of its own and has no owner. Fees go to the destinations of the fee config an intent signs (a hash). The immutable stray config the settlement is constructed with, and the initial FeeDefaults, come from config/fee-configs.json.
_owner: The owner of FeeDefaults, the one privileged role left: it publishes SUGGESTED fee defaults (setDefaults) and can touch no funds, no book and no signed intent. Deploy.s.sol deploys FeeDefaults owned by the signer, publishes the initial defaults, and proposes this address; it must call acceptOwnership from its own key. Recommended: a multisig behind a timelock. The settlement has no owner at all.
_deployers: The keys allowed to SIGN a deploy on this chain. Every broadcasting script in contracts/script/ derives the signer's address from the key forge was handed and refuses to continue unless this list names it. Two entries, because this chain id has two legitimate signers. The first is TESTNET_DEPLOYER_PK, which signs real 943. The second is anvil's first account, published in every foundry document and holding nothing anywhere but a lab: app/scripts/lab/up.sh runs anvil with --chain-id 943 so that every config file in the repository loads unchanged, and it signs the whole protocol up with that account. Listing it here is what keeps the lab working without an environment variable, and it costs nothing — deploying is permissionless, so a stranger holding that published key could already deploy their own settlement to 943 and this list neither grants nor withholds that. Chain 369 lists exactly one address and no anvil account. An empty list, a missing key or a missing file stops the deploy; there is no unset-means-skip. PROVE_DEPLOYER overrides this list and narrows it to one address, never widens it.
_permit2: Permit2, the canonical deterministic deployment. Verified on chain 2026-08-27: 9,152 bytes of code, byte-identical on 369 and 943. A maker who approves this address keeps that approval through every settlement redeploy, which is the whole point of the permit2 rung — ProveRelayer moves and Permit2 does not. The settlement refuses a zero here, so a chain without Permit2 cannot be deployed to until somebody deploys one.
